learned_rules:
- **The money shape rates 8, or 9 if the radar shows the story still climbing and mcap is under ~$1M.** It looks like this: a MIGRATED coin leading on 5m volume, 25–45% off its local high, a printed higher low above the hourly low, 5m flow at or above the hourly pace, more buys than sells, top 10 under 15%, low RugCheck bundles. Both real winners looked like this (CATBOT 4.44x, FLOATER 2.19x, both under $1M) (V1, V6, V13). Rate it what it earns so code sizes it up (owner goal).
- **Owner floor: 7 under ~$1M mcap.** If the hard lines pass, flow is live (5m ≥ $10k and at or above pace), a higher low is printed and the first resistance is ≥1.5x away, rate it 7 or higher. Don't dock points for things the checklist already measured.
- **The MIGRATED buy zone is 10–60% off the local high** (owner rule). Within 10% of the high is a PASS, blocker "chasing" (42 skips: 3 ran, 36 dumped).
- **The shallow band (10–25% off the high) is a breakout trade, capped at 7.** It must be the 5m volume leader, pushing into the high right now, with flow at or above pace. Otherwise PASS, blocker "no breakout".
- **A spike counts as chasing anywhere in the zone.** If the last 5m candle is up more than 25% or 5m volume is more than 3x the hourly pace, wait for a retrace and a printed higher low. Blocker "chasing spike" (PILLSEY).
- **On MIGRATED, flow below pace or no printed higher low is a PASS, never a probe.** A printed higher low means three things: a bounce off the hourly low, a pullback that holds above it, and price back above that bounce's high. A buy share, a fib touch or a first green candle is not one. Blockers "flow below pace" / "no higher low" (Slingoor, ANAKIN, BLUE, SI, AAPLCAT never got past 1.01x).
- **Buy close to the structure.** Enter only within ~12% above the printed higher low, so the thesis breaks before the hard stop. Further above it is a mid-range entry: wait for a pullback or PASS, blocker "mid-range". Stops fill around −30 to −38%, not −20%, so entry distance is the real risk control.
- **Rate on the first resistance (prior high, POC or 0.618).** At ≥1.5x away it can rate 8–9. At 1.3–1.5x the cap is 7. Under 1.3x is a PASS, blocker "target too close" (PAWCAT, SWAN).
- **Above ~$1M mcap, a probe (6) is the most you take.** Only take it if the first resistance is ≥1.5x away and a breakout with flow at or above pace is printing right now. Otherwise PASS, blocker "big cap, no room" (1 green in 10).
- **A migration under 1h old that is still bleeding off its bond spike waits for a base above the hourly low.** Blocker "too new" (50 skips: 9 ran, 41 dumped).
- **In a vamp field, buy only the leader by 5m volume and radar mentions.** A bundle cluster inside a big same-ticker field is a PASS, blocker "split crowd" (V1, V3).
- **A DIP needs all of these:** a 40–70% drawdown, 5m flow at least 0.7x the hourly pace (owner gate, no "rising" needed), the story still on the radar, and a printed higher low with entry within ~12% of it. If all pass, size by conviction (7–8 when clean). A DIP whose catalyst already printed (news, rebrand) is a probe (6) at most until it reclaims its pullback high. A thin tech/LARP story is a PASS, blocker "dead story" (HEXN x2, SIS; DIPs 0 for 5).
- **Hard blocks:** top 10 over 25%, dev over 1%, bundles or insiders over the line, mint or freeze authority live, LP not burned, a political figure, RugCheck danger, any hack/exploit/drain story (V6, V13, V17, owner). Name the blocker in every PASS.
- **If RugCheck didn't load, it's a probe at most (6), not a block.** That needs the dossier's top-10 and dev numbers clean, mcap under $1M and the rest in the money shape. Say bundles are unverified.
- **Manage the trade; stops sell with no review.** If the printed higher low breaks, sell. If it hasn't reached 1.05x by minute 10 with flow under pace, exit. If it's green before initials and 5m volume drops under half the hourly pace, sell half. At the time stop, exit; the only extension is one 15-minute window while a volume surge at or above pace is printing. Re-enter a stopped-out coin only once, and only when it reclaims its prior high with flow at or above pace (re-entries 0 for 4).

rule_changes.evidence: HEXN #2, SIS and AAPLCAT all broke the higher low first and then slid through the stop to -27% to -31%. This exit is set by structure, not by a percent.

daily_reviews.summary: Nothing shows a positive after-cost edge. Across all 93 settled coins the simple plan nets -5.5%: about +4.3% before costs, wiped out by an estimated 9.8% round-trip cost on a $10 buy. With a 1.5x target, a -20% stop and 10% cost, a setup needs about 43% of coins to run just to break even. FINAL_STRETCH (n=20) sits at 45% and nets +1.5%, but its 95% range on that share is roughly 23-67%, and one winner turning into a loser moves the average by about 3 points. That result is probably optimistic anyway: the simulator appears to fill every stop at exactly -20%, while several coins in the logs went to about zero. The routine model logged zero would-buys in 24h (39 brain calls, all PASS), so there is nothing to compare against what it passed on. Its PASSed coins did better than the checklist failures (-3.3% vs -7.1% net), but both groups lose money. Honest answer: no edge yet, and one day of correlated samples can't show one.
findings: Costs are the whole story. All coins: n=93, 30.1% ran, 52.7% dumped, -5.5% net, 9.8% average cost, so about +4.3% before costs. The real trades say the same thing: $18.83 of the $25.79 lost over 22 trades was fees and slippage.

Breakeven math for the simple plan at about 10% cost and no flats: win share p must satisfy p*50 - (1-p)*20 = 10, so p = 42.9%. Only FINAL_STRETCH (45%) clears it. MIGRATED (28.3%) and DIP (15.4%) are nowhere close.
MIGRATED is the biggest bucket and among the worst: n=60, 28.3% ran, 60.0% dumped, -7.5% net. 23.3% of them hit 2x at some point, but the -20% stop usually triggers before the run.
DIP mostly does nothing: n=13, 15.4% ran, 15.4% dumped, so about 69% flat. Net is -7.4%, roughly the cost. Over a 6h window the dips neither recover nor die; they just pay fees.

FINAL_STRETCH: n=20, 45% ran, 55% dumped, 0% flat, +1.5% net, median peak 1.94x. The +1.5% is less than one winner's worth (one winner is about +40 net, or 2 points of the average). Four of the five top runners are FINAL_STRETCH entries, including a pump.fun token named USDC (13.6x) and Chick, entered 2 minutes after launch. If the USDC entry was one of the 1.5x winners and is removed as an impersonator, FINAL_STRETCH drops to about -0.5%.

FINAL_STRETCH's hit-2x share (45%) equals its ran share (45%). If those coins reached 2x before touching -20%, a 2x target would be worth far more than 1.5x. The logs don't show the order, so this has to be tested, not assumed.

Checklist vs brain: checklist_failed n=54, 27.8% ran, -7.1% net. brain_passed n=39, 33.3% ran, -3.3% net. The checklist's rejects were somewhat worse, which is weak support for the checklist. would_buy n=0, so the brain's selection can't be tested.

Over 48h the skip rules blocked 78 coins; 71 have settled: 13 ran (18%), 49 dumped (69%), 9 flat. That is a much higher dump rate than the 53% across all followed coins, so taken together the blocks are earning their keep.

Strongest blocks (small samples): top 10 over 25%: 1 of 11 settled ran, 9 dumped, including rugs (Lucia worst 0.0x, AMS 0.04x). Near the high / chasing: 1 of 7 ran, 6 dumped (GTASZN 0.01x). Falling knife (code): 0 of 4 ran, 4 dumped (RWA 0.02x). Bundles over the line: 0 of 2 ran, 2 dumped. Too new / sniping: 2 of 6 ran, 4 dumped, two of them about zero (BUSTED 0.02x, JASON 0.0x).
RugCheck danger blocked the most: 17 coins, 15 settled, 4 ran (27%), 10 dumped (67%). That ran share is close to the overall baseline, so it isn't clearly hiding winners.

Weak or uncertain blocks: 'falling knife / no higher low' blocked 4 with 1 ran, 0 dumped, 3 flat. 'Dev share over 1%' blocked 2 with 1 ran and 1 pending. Both samples are too small to justify anything, and the dev rule is a hard line anyway.

The top runners are all very young (2 minutes to 1.1h) and small ($16k-$65k market cap). The simple plan caps every win at 1.5x, so a 629x does nothing for its average. Any exit that rides runners will be dominated by one or two coins like MIL; report those results with and without the top coin.
Brain usage: 78 calls in 48h, 0 plan-limit hits, 0 candidates skipped for lack of a brain. Pacing is not the constraint.
rule_ideas: Before any rule comparison, rerun the simulation with stops that can gap: fill at the first sampled price below -20%, plus extra sell slippage on a falling pool. Every rule idea below should be scored that way.

FINAL_STRETCH timing: setup == FINAL_STRETCH and age_hours >= 0.25 and 15k <= mcap <= 35k and 5m volume >= $10k. Report the share that ran, net %, and net with the single best coin removed. Compare against FINAL_STRETCH with age_hours < 0.25 (snipes, which SOUL already rules out).

FINAL_STRETCH exit variant: same entries, target 2x (or sell half at 2x and trail the rest), -20% stop, with the order of target vs stop resolved from the price samples. Reason: hit-2x share = ran share = 45% in this sample.

MIGRATED filter: setup == MIGRATED and 5m volume >= $10k and buy ratio >= 0.55 and flow ratio >= 1.0 and drawdown from high <= 30%. Keep MIGRATED only if some subset clears 43% ran after costs on the full week; otherwise stop trading MIGRATED.

DIP rework: setup == DIP and 40% <= drawdown <= 70% and 5m volume >= 0.5x the hourly pace and buy ratio >= 0.55, with a time stop of 60-90 minutes instead of 6h, since most DIPs were flat and simply paid fees. If no version clears costs, drop DIP.

Impersonation hard block: reject at the market filter when the ticker matches a major or stablecoin (USDC, USDT, SOL, BTC, ETH and similar) on a pump.fun mint (V3, right-token check). Rescore FINAL_STRETCH without these.
Keep these blocks and keep tracking them: top 10 over 25%, near the high / chasing, falling knife (code), bundles over the line, too new / sniping. Each blocked mostly coins that dumped.
Watch only, no change yet: 'falling knife / no higher low' (n=4, 0 dumped). Loosen it only if the full week shows its blocked coins running at or above the baseline share.
Brain test: among checklist == pass, compare brain == would_buy against brain == PASS on share that ran and net %. This needs would-buys to be logged; see data issues.

Cost sensitivity: recompute net % at $20-25 buys where the pool's liquidity allows. If fixed fees (priority, bribe, account rent) make up most of the ~10% cost, the breakeven win share falls a lot. Keep sizing inside the risk budget set by conviction.
data_issues: The simulator appears to fill stops at exactly -20%. The bucket numbers reconcile exactly with that assumption (FINAL_STRETCH: 0.45*50 - 0.55*20 - 10 = +1.5). Yet coins in the skip tables hit 0.0-0.04x (Lucia, AMS, BUSTED, JASON, GTASZN, RWA). If a gap between samples isn't modeled as a gap-through loss, every net % is too high.

would_buy n=0 and not_researched n=0 in 24h, and all 39 brain calls were PASS. Check whether watch-only mode is suppressing BUY verdicts (for example, the prompt saying no buys are allowed) or whether hypothetical buys aren't being written to the log. Without would-buys the main question of this test can't be answered.

The same coin appears more than once, so 93 samples are not 93 independent coins. MIL is in both FINAL_STRETCH and MIGRATED. USDC (Acgs6...) is a top runner and also sits under two skip reasons, 'falling knife (code)' and 'crowd leaving'. Deduplicate by CA, or at least report counts per coin.

Chick (Dueav76...) shows max_x 6.93 in top_runners but best_x 1.66 in the 'too new / sniping' skip table. Either the entry prices or the follow windows differ between the two tables. Reconcile them before using either.
A pump.fun token with the ticker USDC passed the market filters and reached the checklist. Impersonation should be caught at the filter, and its 13.6x currently inflates the FINAL_STRETCH stats.
Top runners don't record which checklist item failed, so there's no way to tell what blocked MIL (629x). Log the failing check on every checklist rejection.

Extreme max_x values need a sanity check against pool liquidity at the peak. MIL's two entries agree on a peak near $14M, so it's probably real, but one-tick spikes in thin pools will distort any runner-based exit test.

The windows don't match: stage and setup stats cover 24h, the skip table covers 48h. 48 coins are still being followed. The ran/dumped thresholds are implied (about 1.5x and 0.8x), not stated in the output.

The labels overlap: 'falling knife (code)' and 'falling knife / no higher low' are separate buckets, and there's an 'other' bucket. Merge them or define them clearly so the rules can be scored cleanly.
The ran_examples and dumped_examples lists stop at 3 (for example, RugCheck danger shows 3 of 4 runners), so the counts can't be checked from this output.
The summary isn't broken out by 5m volume, flow ratio, buy ratio or drawdown. Confirm these are logged per coin at the moment of entry, not filled in later, before the rule tests.
One 24h window is one market regime. Coins launched in the same hours move together, so the effective sample is smaller than n. The scheduled Nov 10 review date has passed; use the full logged week.

daily_reviews.summary: Nothing shows a positive edge after costs. Over 309 settled coins, every setup lost money net: FINAL_STRETCH -7.2%, DIP -7.4%, MIGRATED -13.5%. Costs alone averaged 9.8% per round trip. Before costs, FINAL_STRETCH made about +2.9% and DIP about +1.8%, but at n=46 and n=54 the noise is roughly ±4–5 points, so neither is different from zero. With a 1.5x / -20% plan and ~10% costs, you need about 43% of coins to reach 1.5x before -20% just to break even. The best group (FINAL_STRETCH) managed 32.6%, and the error bar on that is about ±14 points. The routine model gave zero would-buys, so the "did its buys beat its passes" question can't be answered. It passed on all 164 coins it reviewed. Those coins averaged -11.7% net, about the same as the checklist rejects at -11.3%, so passing on everything was roughly right this day, even though it missed LMAO, Marvin and WIGGLES.
findings: Costs are the main problem. Average round-trip cost was 9.8% on a $10 buy, and the average net was -11.5%, so the coins themselves lost only about 1.7% before costs. This matches the real trades before the pause, where fees and slippage ($18.83) were 2.7x the price loss ($6.96).

FINAL_STRETCH (n=46) was the best setup and still lost: 32.6% ran, 26.1% hit 2x, median peak 1.44x, net -7.2% on 10.1% cost. A 95% interval on the run share is about 19–46%, which doesn't reach the ~43% break-even.

DIP (n=54) dumped least (33.3%), but most of these coins just went flat (about 54% neither ran nor dumped). Only 13.0% ran and net was -7.4% on 9.2% cost. Before costs it roughly breaks even; costs make it a loser.

MIGRATED (n=209) is the bulk of the flow and the worst setup: 17.2% ran, 66.0% dumped, net -13.5%. Even so, 3 of the 5 top runners were MIGRATED coins under 0.3h old, so these young migrations swing both ways.

Brain vs checklist: coins the brain reviewed and passed on (n=164) ran more often than checklist rejects (23.8% vs 13.1%) but also dumped much more (70.7% vs 49.0%). Net was the same (-11.7% vs -11.3%). The checklist sends the brain more volatile coins, not better ones after costs.

Filters that are earning their keep (48h, settled coins only): 'falling knife (code)' saw 10 of 11 dump and 1 run. 'too new / sniping' saw 28 of 34 dump (82%). 'flow below pace' saw 26 of 34 dump (76%). 'near the high / chasing' saw 20 of 26 dump (77%). 'bundles over the line' saw 0 of 7 run.

Filters that barely sort winners from losers: 'top 10 over 25%' had 7 of 34 run (21%) and 23 dump (68%), close to the all-coin average (18.8% ran, 60.5% dumped). 'RugCheck danger' had 7 of 25 run (28%), slightly better than average. These are hard lines or close to them, so they stay. A rug skips the stop, and one 6-hour window can't show the tail risk.
'falling knife / no higher low' (n=10 settled: 3 ran, 4 dumped, 3 flat) and 'dev share over 1%' (n=5: 2 ran) are too small to judge either way. The dev rule is a hard line regardless.

The top runners list is survivorship by construction: 5 out of 309. It doesn't support any rule. LMAO (19.6x), Marvin (10.6x) and WIGGLES (8.0x) were all brain PASS, but so were 164 coins that averaged -11.7%.
rule_ideas: Cost gate: skip any coin whose estimated round-trip cost_pct is above 5%, then re-run every setup on the coins that remain. If no setup's before-cost result is above the remaining cost, that setup is dead at $10 size. Also simulate $25 and $50 buys to see whether the cost drag is mostly fixed fees.

FINAL_STRETCH candidate: setup=FINAL_STRETCH AND checklist passed AND 5m volume >= $10k AND buy ratio >= 0.55 AND flow ratio (5m vs hourly pace) >= 1.0. Before trusting it, require n >= 40 settled and a net above 0 with costs included.

DIP candidate: setup=DIP AND drawdown from high 40–70% AND peak mcap >= $70k AND flow ratio >= 1.0 AND buy ratio >= 0.55. The aim is to test whether coins with the crowd still arriving escape the 54% flat bucket. Run deeper drawdowns (>70%) as a separate bucket, not mixed in.

Young MIGRATED split: setup=MIGRATED AND age_hours < 0.5 AND mcap 30k–150k AND 5m volume >= $10k, compared against MIGRATED with age 0.5–12h. The question is whether the fat right tail pays for the 66% dump rate after costs. Score each bucket by mean net, not by hit rate.

Exit-plan comparison on the same logged coins: 1.5x/-20% vs 2x/-30% vs Trencher's real plan (sell initials at 2x, break-even stop after 1.3x, trailing stop on the rest). For a 1.5x/-20% plan to be worth running, a subset needs a first-touch 1.5x rate of at least ~43% at 10% cost (~36% at 5% cost).

Brain calibration: when the brain says PASS, also log its conviction (1–10). Then test whether brain conviction >= 5 coins beat brain conviction <= 3 coins on net %. That lets you grade the brain even when it makes no buys.

Keep as-is and keep watching: 'falling knife (code)', 'too new / sniping', 'flow below pace' and 'near the high'. Loosen one only if, at n >= 30 settled, the coins it blocked net out better than the coins it let through.
data_issues: Peak numbers disagree for the same contract address. In top_runners, rockstar max_x is 14.53 while skips_48h has best_x 1.95. twert is 14.72 vs 1.81, and WIGGLES is 8.01 vs 1.69. Nearly every skip best_x falls between 1.5 and 1.95, which looks like the price at the first sample after the 1.5x take-profit fired rather than the true peak. Label best_x as the exit-sample price, or recompute it. Separately, check the 19.6x and 14.7x peaks against a second price source for bad ticks.

Gap handling in the simple plan is unclear. Dumped examples have worst_x of 0.0, 0.01 and 0.02. If the sim credits these at -20% instead of the next sampled price, the dump-side losses are understated and the true net is worse than reported. Confirm which price is used.

'ran' and 'dumped' overlap. FINAL_STRETCH shows 32.6% + 67.4% = 100% with no flat coins, so 'dumped' probably means 'touched -20% at any point' rather than 'exited at the stop'. Switch to mutually exclusive first-touch labels (TP first, stop first, neither).

'ran' is almost the same as 'hit 2x': overall 18.8% vs 17.5%, and exactly equal for DIP (13.0/13.0) and checklist_failed (13.1/13.1). Either the definitions overlap or price sampling is so coarse that coins jump from below 1.5x to above 2x between samples. Log the sampling interval and the time to first touch.

would_buy n=0 in 24h. Either the brain issued 0 BUYs out of 164 decisions, or watch-only mode isn't recording would-buys. If it's the first, next week won't produce any data on the brain's selection skill. Log the brain's conviction score and a would-buy-at-threshold flag on every decision.
The stage name 'brain_passed' is ambiguous. Here it means the brain said PASS, not that the coin got past the brain. Rename it, for example to 'brain_declined'.

The skip reasons overlap and the windows don't match. The same coin appears under several reasons (ANT under both top10 and flow; USDC under both falling knife and fading volume), so blocked counts are double-counted. The skips cover 48h while the main stats cover 24h. Report each coin's primary block reason, or a deduplicated count.

The cost model needs checking against reality. 9.8% on a $10 buy should be compared with the 22 real paper trades' fees per dollar. Record the cost split (fixed fees vs pool slippage) per coin, so the cost gate and size tests in rule_ideas can be run.

This summary doesn't break results down by mcap, age, 5m volume, flow ratio, buy ratio or drawdown. Those buckets are needed to pre-screen any of the rule ideas. Add them to the daily rollup, with n per bucket.

daily_reviews.summary: No edge yet. All 322 settled coins lost money after costs on the simple plan, and so did every setup: the average was -13.8%, of which about 9.9% was round-trip cost, so the price moves alone already lost about 4%. With a +50% target, a -20% stop and about 10% cost, a winner nets about +40% and a loser about -30%, so a setup has to reach 1.5x before the stop roughly 43% of the time just to break even. The best bucket, FINAL_STRETCH, did it 27.7% of the time (n=47). The overall average is clearly negative: about ±3.6 points of noise at n=322. Even FINAL_STRETCH's -10.6% has a 95% range of roughly ±9 points that stays below zero, and the real sample is smaller than it looks because of meta clustering (GTA and FIONA copies) and at least one coin logged twice. The routine model made zero would-buys, so there is nothing to compare against what it passed on. The 79 coins it reviewed and passed did -14.4%, the same as the 168 the checklist failed (-14.0%). On this data neither the checklist nor the model separates winners from losers.
findings: Overall (n=322): 19.3% reached 1.5x before the -20% stop, 68.6% hit the stop, the median coin peaked at only 1.24x, average net -13.8% with 9.9% average cost. The typical coin's best move barely covers costs twice over.

The simple plan's result is roughly ran% × +40 − dumped% × 30. For all coins that gives 0.193×40 − 0.686×30 ≈ -12.9%, close to the measured -13.8%. The losses come from the hit rate, not from a few bad outliers.

FINAL_STRETCH (n=47) is the least bad: 27.7% ran, 25.5% hit 2x, median peak 1.38x, net -10.6%. That is still well short of the ~43% ran rate needed to break even. MIGRATED (n=222): 20.7% ran, net -13.1%.

DIP is the worst setup (n=53): 5.7% ran, median peak 1.14x, net -19.9%. More DIP coins hit 2x at some point (9.4%) than hit 1.5x before the -20% stop (5.7%), so the stop often fired before a later run. Even so, nothing here justifies buying dips: they mostly did not bounce.

Checklist failures (n=168): 17.3% ran, 64.9% dumped, net -14.0%. Coins the model reviewed and passed (n=79): 21.5% ran, 74.7% dumped, 24.1% hit 2x, net -14.4%. Passing the checklist gave a wider spread of outcomes (more 2x, more dumps) but no better average.
Would-buys: n=0. The model passed on every coin it reviewed, so the question of whether its picks beat its passes cannot be answered from this data.

48h skip reasons look like they are earning their keep. Coins blocked by each rule reached 1.5x less often than the 19.3% baseline: top 10 over 25% 9/66 (13.6%, 79% dumped), falling knife (code) 6/48 (12.5%, 85% dumped), RugCheck danger 4/29 (13.8%, with dumps to 0.01-0.03x), too new 1/9. The blocked coins that did run mostly peaked at 1.5-1.75x, barely past the target. Nothing here argues for loosening a rule.
The 'other' skip bucket (n=12) holds the best blocked runners: CALICO 3.25x, After 2.36x, Ant 2.32x. Three wins in 12 is noise, and the block reason itself isn't recorded.

Top runners are all very young: ages 2.5-29 minutes, market caps $18k-$186k, and 3 of 5 failed the checklist. Their peaks (8-25x) are survivorship highlights. The simple plan sells at 1.5x, and the stats show such runs are rare (1-2% of coins).

Meta crowding: many GTA VI copies (GTA, GTAVI, GTA6, GTASZN, GTAB, PolyGTA, GTAKID, LUCIA, Leonida) and at least six different FIONA contract addresses. Almost all of them dumped, which is the vamp pattern from V1/V13. FIONA copies also include two of the top runners, so a coin name alone doesn't tell you which one is the original.

Cost is the biggest single drag. About 10% round trip on a $10 buy is half the -20% stop distance and a fifth of the +50% target. That matches the live result before the pause: $18.83 of the $25.79 loss was fees and slippage.
rule_ideas: Set every rule's thresholds before looking at the week's data, then score them on a holdout of days the rule wasn't tuned on. For any rule to be worth testing live, its subset needs n ≥ 40 and an average net whose 95% lower bound is above 0. Anything else counts as noise.

Cost gate: only count coins whose estimated round-trip cost is ≤ 5% (if per-coin cost isn't logged, use mcap ≥ $100k as a stand-in). Compare net % with the ≤5% and >5% cost groups side by side. The idea: with a 1.24x median peak, a coin only has room for profit if its pool is deep.

FINAL_STRETCH-only test: setup = FINAL_STRETCH AND checklist = pass AND 5m volume ≥ $10k AND buy ratio ≥ 0.55 AND flow ratio ≥ 1.0. Score it on both the simple plan and a 2x target / -35% stop / 60-minute time stop.

Exit-shape test on all setups: compare +50%/-20% with 2x/-35% and 2x/-50% (all with a 6h time exit). The DIP numbers (more coins hit 2x than 1.5x-before-stop) suggest the -20% stop sits inside normal noise; 68.6% of all coins hit it.

DIP suspension test: drop DIP entirely, or allow it only when drawdown is 40-55% AND 5m volume ≥ its 1h average pace (flow ratio ≥ 1.0) AND buy ratio ≥ 0.55. Check whether any DIP subset gets above a 25% ran rate. If none does, retire the setup.

Meta-crowding rule: if 3 or more coins sharing a name root (GTA*, FIONA*) were logged in the last 6h, only consider the one with the highest mcap and 5m volume and skip the rest as vamps (V1). Test whether the coins it would skip did worse than the one it would keep.

Young-MIGRATED test: setup = MIGRATED AND age < 0.5h AND mcap $30k-$200k AND 5m volume ≥ $10k AND checklist = pass. The top runners cluster here, but so do rugs. Only adopt it if the net average beats MIGRATED as a whole (-13.1%) by more than its noise.

Model-score test (this needs a logging change first): in watch-only mode, have the model record a conviction score from 0 to 10 for every checklist-pass coin, not just PASS. Then test whether coins scored 7+ beat coins scored under 5 on net %. Without that, the week can't evaluate the model at all.
Do not loosen any hard line. Top 10 over 25%, RugCheck danger, dev over 1% and too new all blocked coins that ran less often than the baseline; RugCheck's blocked coins included dumps to 0.01-0.03x.
data_issues: Stage coverage has a gap. 168 checklist failures plus 79 model passes is 247 coins, but 322 settled, so 75 coins have no stage. At the same time 'not_researched' shows n=0, even though 1,353 candidates were skipped with no model call in 48h. Either the skipped candidates aren't followed (a selection bias) or they are being put in the wrong bucket.

The model was blind most of the time: 194 of 327 calls (59%) hit the plan limit and 1,353 candidates got no review. The 79 coins it did review are whatever got through the rate limit, not a random sample. Pace the calls or put them in order of priority before the week's comparison means anything.
Zero would-buys. Either watch-only mode pushes the model toward PASS, or no coin cleared its bar. The logs need a hypothetical verdict and conviction score for every reviewed coin.

Same contract address, conflicting results: 'apocry ' HVxXzEt87... shows max_x 8.27 (top runners, 24h) and best_x 1.0 / worst 0.72 'dumped' (falling-knife skips, 48h). Either the coin was logged twice with different start points or best_x is calculated differently in the two places. Deduplicate per address (keep the first observation) before any stats.

The 'dumped' label doesn't match -20%: coins with worst_x 0.79 (LUCIA, STF, Neko, BUCKME), 0.78 and 0.76 are marked dumped. Document whether the threshold includes costs, and keep 'ran' and 'dumped' consistent with the simple plan's exits.
Mixed windows: the skip table covers 48h while every other table covers 24h, so the numbers can't be reconciled directly.
The 'other' skip reason (12 coins, including the 3 best blocked runners) isn't categorized. Log the actual reason.

Outlier to verify: RUGGED, MIGRATED at $30.9k mcap only 3.6 minutes old, peaked at 24.8x. Check the pool and pair, token decimals and the price source before trusting it. Its net is capped by the 1.5x exit, but it distorts the top-runner list.
The top-runner and skip records don't include 5m volume, flow ratio, buy ratio, drawdown or per-coin cost, so none of the rule ideas can be checked on this summary. Include them in the export.
Sampling interval isn't recorded. Some coins peaked within 28-34 minutes, and the 'both crossed, count the loss' rule depends on how often prices were sampled.
Timeline: watch-only was set for about one week from Nov 3, with the test planned around Nov 10. Today is Nov 20. Confirm whether the pause was extended and which dates the final test dataset covers.
Naming: 'brain_passed' means the model reviewed the coin and its verdict was PASS (no buy). Rename it to avoid reading it as approved.
